subject: Identify a polygon on a map based on user clicks

messages.author: 7d8098941e716702
messages.subject: Identify a polygon on a map based on user clicks
parts:
I recently used shiny and ggplot2 to build an interactive application. One of the output tab shows a heat map (below please find a made-up example)

library(maps)
library(ggplot2)
state_map <- map_data("state")
spatial_data <- data.frame(region=tolower(state.name),
                           area=state.area)
spatial_data <- merge(spatial_data, state_map, by="region")
spatial_data <- spatial_data[order(spatial_data$order),]
p<-ggplot(spatial_data,
          aes(x=long, y=lat, group=group, fill=area)) +
  geom_polygon() + coord_equal()
print(p)

There are about 50 states on the map. Is there any way for a user to locate the state polygons by clicks (i..e, shiny will tell the user which state she/he has clicked on)? The map is a dynamic map based on user data inputs (i.e., the colors may change).

plotOutput can help us to identify the x-axis and y-axis of the clicks, but it is design for plot rather than ggplot2. Am I right?
 
Thanks!
Dingxi

messages.author: 889de486273d901d
messages.subject: Re: Identify a polygon on a map based on user clicks
parts:
I don't think there is any practical way to do what you want as long as you use ggplot2 to do your plotting.  Various people have suggested ways to use locator() and friends go from a mouse click in screen coordinates to user coordinates on a graph drawn with ggplot, but I've personally never gotten them to work.   

In my experience, if you want to interact with a graph, you have to use base graphics and not ggplot.  Presumably the new gvis package fixes this - draws great graphics, with the same incremental process of building a plot and is highly interactive, but I haven't use it yet.
